text:
alina: FYI I ran an nsys capture on A100-80GB with the small-batcher workload. Seeing periodic 20-40ms spikes during decode, correlated with repeated workspace alloc/free around matmul. Trace attached (perfetto/NSYS).

mike: Can you paste the timeline excerpt and the algo ids being selected?

alina: Timeline excerpt (nsys timeline view):
```
[0.120s] cudamalloc(64MB) -> cublasLtWorkspaceAlloc(64MB) -> cuBLASLtMatmul(algo=7, 12.3ms)
[0.144s] cudafree(64MB)
[0.620s] cudamalloc(64MB) -> cublasLtWorkspaceAlloc(64MB) -> cuBLASLtMatmul(algo=7, 11.8ms)
[0.644s] cudafree(64MB)
...
```
This pattern repeats every request when batch size is 1-2. Algo id is 7 consistently for the short matmuls.

vikram: That pattern screams workspace churn. Algo 7 requires ~64MB workspace for these shapes. If we are allocating per-request instead of reusing a slab that's expensive. Might be a change in the algo probe that started preferring higher-FLOP algos for short runs.

alina: Runtime note: our probe currently picks algo by measured throughput (FLOPs) without factoring workspace penalty. For tiny batches that ends up picking algo with large workspace which forces alloc/free. We also set workspace_size=0 by default and only allocate when algo requests it.

perf-bot: regression alert: matmul_workspace_alloc_rate increased 3.8x since deploy 2026-03-15. Top contributor: small-batcher route. See /perf/alerts/1958

sam: Quick mitigation: two low-risk options:
1) Pre-allocate a per-stream workspace slab and reuse between matmuls (reduces cuda malloc/free).
2) Add a workspace cap to the algo filter for the small-path, e.g.:
```json
{"matmul_algo_filter": {"max_workspace_bytes": 16777216}}
```
Either should reduce spikes.

mike: Can you reproduce this in CI or locally with a deterministic workload? Link to perfetto/NSYS capture would help.

alina: Repro'd in CI with --batcher=continuous-small and nsys profile. Perfetto shows many cublasLtWorkspaceAlloc + cudaMalloc calls preceding the matmul kernel. Perfetto slice sample: 
```
slice 120.124s: cudaMalloc(67108864) 4.2ms
slice 120.129s: cublasLtMatmul(algo=7) 12.1ms
slice 120.141s: cudaFree(67108864) 2.1ms
```
When batcher groups requests (batch>8) the probe prefers algos with zero workspace or smaller workspace and spikes go away.

vikram: Proposed fix: change algo selection heuristic to penalize workspace > 16MB for matmuls with rows/cols < 2k (heuristic: workspace_penalty = workspace_bytes / 1e6). Also add a fallback that pins algos for the small-batcher path. I'll open a PR with tests.

dani: Also saw KV-cache warmup interactions: when prefix length toggles we re-allocate cached tensors which sometimes bumps the matmul shapes and triggers different algos mid-rollout. Suggest we skip expensive probe during first N requests (warmup) for a given route.

mike: Sounds good. Alina, can you try pre-alloc slab and set workspace cap in a canary? We'll monitor alloc_rate and p90 latency.

alina: On it — will deploy a canary with slab reuse + max_workspace_bytes=16MB to dedicated small-batcher pool. I'll post NSYS captures after canary.

mike: :thumbsup: thanks. If the canary looks clean, let's ship the heuristic change and add a regression alert to catch workspace alloc spikes next time.
